evidence_note: cdyn Game Features: 'roto feature — United's answer to Bally's magic squares, the eight numbers forming a square around the center number of the 5x5 main card could be rotated around.' No catalog gameplay-feature covers this; distinct from roto-targets (flipper-game mechanism). Would need research into which United bingos carry it.

IPDB 1254 Notable Features: 'Backglass stop-motion light animation (Humpty Dumpty falls).' Named in 0253's backbox-light-animations description; the uncarried-link warning on that record is this missing attachment.

target: lady-robin-hood, cinderella, jack-n-jill + rest of the seven-game fairy-tale series
evidence_note: Wikipedia (Humpty Dumpty, Design): 'The game is the first in a series of seven Fairy Tale games, all of which include an backglass animation.' Each machine's own IPDB entry should confirm before attaching.

pinrepair Gottlieb EM list: 'Jones, 11/49, 800 produced, A-, light animated train on backglass, 1 kick-out hole.' IPDB 1399 (K. C. Jones) notable features carry no animation mention, so IPDB alone would not surface it. Left out of 0253 prose because the record carries no backbox feature.

IPDB 966 Toys: 'A talking head named "Rudy".' Named in 0254's toys description; the uncarried-link warning on that record is this missing attachment. Rudy moves and is shot into (midnight mouth shot), so interactive; arguably animatronic-toys too.
IPDB 20 Toys: ''Thing' hand - ball capture device.' Named in 0254's toys and ball-holding-toys descriptions; both uncarried-link warnings are this missing attachment.

claimed_value: ball-holding-toys (gumball machine); static-toys or interactive-toys (working analog clock — judge on research)
evidence_note: Wikipedia glossary, toy entry: 'Twilight Zone features two significant toys: The gumball machine (which stores and releases balls), and a working analog clock'. Named in 0254's toys description.

Wikipedia (Design and layout): castle centerpiece with drawbridge/portcullis battered by shots; 'two Trolls, animated targets that are normally concealed below the playfield' that 'can pop up during certain gameplay modes'. Named in 0254's toys and pop-up-toys descriptions.
Wikipedia (Design): the large saucer 'placed above a set of targets at the top center of the playfield, can shake and flash in time with the player's success'. Named in 0254's bash-toys description.
IPDB 4059: 'The Ringmaster is an animated head that elevates from the underside of the playfield'. Named in 0254's pop-up-toys description.

claimed_value: bash-toys (motorized collapsing skyscraper); godzilla-pro gets static-toys (static building) — verify per model
evidence_note: Stern Godzilla feature matrix: 'Premium and LE models feature a motorized collapsing skyscraper building bash toy'; Pro row: 'Static skyscraper building with intersecting ramps and virtual ball lock'. Named in 0254's toys description.

claimed_value: bash-toys (Leatherface Kill Door); ball-holding-toys (Meat Grinding Ball Lock) — verify which models
evidence_note: Spooky product page: 'an interactive Leatherface Kill Door Bash Toy, and a Meat Grinding Ball Lock Mechanism'. Named in 0254's bash-toys description.

Wikipedia (Design): 'Notable features on the playfield include four mechanized Martian figures'; IPDB 3781 Toys: 'four dancing Martian figures (for Martian Attack...)'. Left out of the bash-toys attachment pass, which covered the saucer only.

IPDB 4059: 'The Ringmaster is an animated head that elevates from the underside of the playfield and makes wise cracks at the player'. Attached as pop-up-toys and bash-toys; the animated/speaking half is unattached.

claimed_value: no leaf fits — static-toys and animatronic-toys both wrong
evidence_note: IPDB 2684 Toys: 'Working analog clock; tells time in attract mode, times most modes during game play.' Not static (it moves and drives mode timing), not animatronic (no figure gesturing or speaking). interactive-toys would fit but is a grouping node the feature-grouping-node lint forbids attaching. Needs either a new leaf for game-driven non-figure props or a decision to stretch animatronic-toys.

claimed_value: pop-up-toys (Victim Clawing Out Of Freezer); animatronic-toys (360-degree Whirling Leatherface)
evidence_note: Spooky product page mech list: 'Victim Clawing Out Of Freezer Reactive Pop Up Mechanism' and '360 Physical Whirling Leatherface Mechanism'. These sit in the Collector's Edition bullet list rather than the game-level paragraph, so per-edition carriage needs confirming; only the CE product page is in the web cache.

claimed_value: same toy attachments as the originals — verify per remake
evidence_note: The originals now carry their toy features; the Chicago Gaming, Pedretti and American Pinball remakes of the same games carry none. Remakes reproduce the playfield mechs but each needs its own source before asserting, and Funhouse 2.0 (Rudy's Nightmare) is a reworked game rather than a straight remake.
The 2021 Pro/Premium/LE models are attached; the 2024 70th Anniversary model of the same title carries nothing. The 2021 feature matrix does not cover it, so it needs its own source.

target: the-x-files, the-sopranos, nascar (and other Sega/Stern UK-market builds 1997-2005)
claimed_value: center-up-posts (UK All-Skill centre post) — and outlane up-posts, for which no record exists
evidence_note: Pinball News 'It's in the post': the UK All-Skill system fitted two outlane up-posts plus 'a large centre up-post between the flippers', player-worked by a second pair of flipper buttons, from The X Files (1997, Sega) through The Sopranos (2005, Stern), ending at NASCAR when the new siderail ruled out the extra buttons. The catalog holds only the general-market builds, so the three uncarried-link warnings on 0255's center-up-posts description are this gap. Two questions for the user: (a) should UK builds be separate models, or the feature attached to the existing ones? (b) the outlane up-post has no gameplay-feature record at all.

target: blocking gate / safety gate (V-shaped ball saver between the flippers, 1950-1951)
evidence_note: IPDB glossary, Blocking Gate: 'The metal, V-shaped ball-saving device that would raise and lower between flippers on some Gottlieb and Chicago Coin games during 1950-1951 ... It is the precedessor of the round plastic Up-post used in 1960's games and later. Gottlieb also referred to this device as a Safety Gate. An example of this feature can be found on Chicago Coin's 1951 'Thing'.' No catalog record covers it; 0255's center-up-posts description names Thing as the ancestor's carrier, which is the uncarried-link warning on that record. Needs a per-machine sweep of 1950-51 Gottlieb and Chicago Coin games.

IPDB glossary, Drop lane: 'A game having two of these lanes is Bally's 1968 Dixieland where the left one is very long and has a detour gate in its path, if earned by the player.' Dixieland (1968, Bally) carries neither feature in the catalog; named in 0259's drop-lanes description, which is the uncarried-link warning there. The glossary entry also points at a full IPDB game list for the feature, worth mining for the rest of the drop-lane population.

claimed_value: free ball gate (upper right) — no upper-right-free-ball-gates record exists; also 2-way kick-out hole, rotating pop-bumper turntable, mini-post screws
evidence_note: IPDB 4561 Notable Features lists 'Upper right free ball gate' and describes the bonus sequence in which 'the Free Ball Gate delivers it back to the shooter lane'. The model carries no gate feature at all, which is the uncarried-link warning on 0257's free-ball-gates description. free-ball-gates has one modelled child (right-outlane-free-ball-gates); an upper-right sibling is missing.

Turner's own ruleset (p.9, Kickback/Shadow Lanes): 'The Grappling Hook Kickback serves as a ball save on the left outlane when lit.' The reserve page lists 'One Outlane Kickback' among the playfield features. Not attached in the catalog, so 0256's left-outlane-kickbacks description had to reach for an older machine instead of the current one.

All 16 models carrying the outholes feature are recorded by IPDB as having 'Two outhole troughs' or 'Two outholes', but every model_gameplay_features row has a NULL count. Since every pinball machine has an outhole, the record only means anything as a count; without it the vocabulary reads as if these games alone have outholes. Either backfill count=2 or rename the record.

IPDB 33 Notable Features: 'Left kickback lane, Left dual outlanes, Left outlane detour gate, Right-side free ball return lane.' The model carries left-kickback-lanes and detour-gates but not dual-outlanes, and 'Right-side free ball return lane' has no side-specific record either.
